speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when these gait and limb coordination problems first started and if they have been getting progressively worse?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any recent headaches, double vision, or difficulty swallowing? Do you have a history of cancer or autoimmune conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any new visual disturbances, speech difficulties, or sensory changes like numbness or tingling? I also need to know if you have experienced any fever or signs of infection recently, as this is crucial given your immunosuppressive therapy.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI_with_contrast
Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, I am highly concerned about progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), so I need to see the MRI results immediately.
